metadata.note: The Troy and Greenfield Railroad (chartered in Massachusetts 1848) and the Hoosac Tunnel: Greenfield - Shelburne Falls - Charlemont - Hoosac Tunnel - North Adams - Williamstown - the Vermont line, with the Southern Vermont (Pownal) that the T&G bought in 1860. The T&G company never ran a train, so no feature carries it as operator: the line is drawn by who ran the trains -- the Troy and Boston on the west end (1859-1887), the Vermont and Massachusetts on the east end (1868-1875), the Commonwealth of Massachusetts's State Manager (1875-1880; through the tunnel from 1876), the Fitchburg by State contract (1880-1887) and as owner (1887-1900), and the Boston and Maine (1900-1958), plus one Amtrak excursion in 2015. One feature per drawable span x operator (CLAUDE.md Rule 4 splits share geometry). Built from research/branches/troy_and_greenfield_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-16).

'Vermont and Massachusetts Railroad' (#5E8C31) and 'Commonwealth of Massachusetts' (#B08D1A) had no features in data/; their new colours were checked programmatically to be unused by any other company. A later V&M / Fitchburg main (Fitchburg - Athol - Millers Falls - Greenfield) should reuse these.
omitted: Report block [3], Greenfield - Hoosac Tunnel 1874 - 30 Jun 1875 under a NOT-ESTABLISHED operator (the V&M was under Fitchburg lease from 1874): drawable only once an operator is named; folded into the V&M feature as the report advises, with the caveat in its note. No year is lost.
Report block [10], the stage coach over Hoosac Mountain 1868-1876: not rail. The tunnel is not drawn for any year before 1876.

Report block [11], New Haven and Northampton / New Haven trains Conway Junction - Shelburne Falls over T&G rails: a New Haven service, belongs to the New Haven's Northampton / Canal Line file (only a 1904 [ANCHOR] is drawable there).

Pownal (Vermont) after 1887: no feature -- which of the two paired tracks carried passenger trains after the Fitchburg took both is unresolved (report UNRESOLVED 3); the BHT&W layer already draws the surviving track 1879-1958.
Everything after 30 Dec 1958 except the 2015 excursion: freight only (Rule 1).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1: every feature ends at its last passenger year or operator change; the tunnel is drawn from 1876 because 1875 traffic through the bore was freight; post-1958 freight (B&M, Guilford / Pan Am, Pan Am Southern, CSX) is mentioned in notes only; the 2015 Amtrak excursion is a one-year [ANCHOR] under mode tourist_rail.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Built to Rule 5: steam from opening (1859 / 1868), electric in the tunnel c.1911-1946. Nothing trimmed. The 1868-1876 stage over the mountain is road transport and is not drawn.
metadata.line_label_audit: Built to Rule 6: each label names the operator that ran the trains in that feature's years; 'Troy and Greenfield' is never used as an operator.
not_yet_sourced: Who ran the trains on Greenfield - Hoosac Tunnel from the 1874 Fitchburg lease of the V&M to 30 Jun 1875 (drawn as V&M), and how much of 1875-1880 traffic was the State's own trains versus the Fitchburg's (V&M Division) through trains on tolls (drawn as the Commonwealth) -- report UNRESOLVED 1. Best sources: the State Manager's annual reports and the Railroad Commissioners' reports 1874-1880.
First through passenger train via the tunnel: drawn from 1876; if a primary 1875 passenger timetable via the tunnel turns up, commonwealth-hoosac-tunnel-north-adams could start 1875 (UNRESOLVED 2).

The two parallel tracks through Pownal from 1879: which surviving track is the T&B's and which the BHT&W's, and when each lost passenger trains (UNRESOLVED 3). The T&B feature draws the surviving one.
The MA/VT state-line milepost, and so the exact lengths of the west-end features (UNRESOLVED 4).
The 1958 end day west of Greenfield: 30 Dec (Wikipedia, American-Rails) vs 28 Nov (American-Rails Hoosac reference); year agreed (UNRESOLVED 5).
The Troy and Boston's arrangement with the State for North Adams - State Line 1862-1875 (UNRESOLVED 6).
The month of the 1880 State operating contracts (Acts 1880 c.261).
Headways are estimates except 1868-69 (two trains each way, sourced) (UNRESOLVED 8).
Post-1958 excursions other than Oct 2015 not searched in depth; Amtrak's 'first in 30 years' implies a c.1985 special not found (UNRESOLVED 9). The 2015 year itself rests on secondary/photo sources.

THIS FEATURE: North Adams - Greylock - Blackinton - Williamstown - MA/VT line - Pownal - North Pownal - VT/NY line, traced 13.6 mi against c. 6.6 mi North Adams - state line (JF-SNE 27, state-line milepost not printed) plus c. 7-8 mi through Pownal (report block [4]); trace: North Adams - MA/VT line 6.8 mi, MA/VT line - end 6.7 mi. In Massachusetts it is on the surviving main. In VERMONT, from the MA/VT line to just past North Pownal, it is drawn on the SAME surviving track that boston_hoosac_tunnel_and_western_railway.geojson draws for the BHT&W / Fitchburg / B&M (1879-1958). From 1879 two parallel tracks ran here, and which survives is unresolved (report UNRESOLVED 3; the BHT&W layer infers the survivor is the BHT&W-built one). OSM maps no T&B grade in Pownal (railway~abandoned|razed|demolished queried directly: the only abandoned ways in the valley east of the main are the Bennington branch grade towards Bennington, not this road). So for 1859-1887 this may be the OTHER company's alignment a few tens of metres from the T&B's own, and from 1879 it overlaps the BHT&W feature on identical geometry. The last 1.3 mi (2.1 km) is the abandoned OSM way 'old B&M alignment' (way 1047144657, the Troy & Boston grade) into New York; the line ends on the existing troy-boston-hoosick-valley feature's last vertex but one (-73.2904, 42.8197), where that feature leaves the traced grade for a c. 1 mi straight stub to its own end point. WEST-END RELOCATION (Rule 2): WS76 says the State Manager rebuilt the line from the state line to the 'little tunnel' by 1 Jul 1876; the 1859-1876 trains may in places have run on an earlier alignment than the one drawn.

segments.note: Report blocks [1], [6b] and [4], merged as the report recommends: Troy and Boston trains ran Troy - Hoosick - (Southern Vermont, Pownal) - Williamstown - North Adams throughout. First passengers 1859: an eight-car excursion of stockholders and guests from Troy over 'the Troy and North Adams railroad' on Wed 8 Jun 1859 (Springfield Weekly Republican 11 Jun 1859) and a 42-car Sunday-school excursion North Adams - Troy in Sep 1859 (SWR 3 Sep 1859); the month of the first regular train is not established, the year is. Anchors 1869 (Worcester Daily Spy 10 Jul 1869 V&M advertisement: 'Leave Troy at 8.00 a m, North Adams at 5.40 and 10.15 a m, (by stage over Mountain)') and 1884-85 (through Pullman cars 'to Eagle Bridge, Hoosac Junction, North Adams, Greenfield', Indianapolis Journal 2 Apr 1885). Ownership: the Troy and Greenfield, which never ran trains, leased this end to the T&B (Wikipedia: 1856) and bought the Southern Vermont (Pownal) on 21 Apr 1860 (NCS); the Commonwealth of Massachusetts took the property as mortgagee 13 Oct 1862 and from 1 Jul 1875 put it under a State Manager, but no State operation of trains west of North Adams was found, so the T&B is the operator throughout (under what arrangement 1862-1875 is not established). From 1880 the T&B and the Boston, Hoosac Tunnel and Western held the State's contract 'for operating that portion west of North Adams' (Governor's message, 9 Feb 1887). Ends at the consolidation of the State road into the Fitchburg, 1 Feb 1887. The Pownal (Vermont) miles are lower confidence than the Massachusetts miles: the June 1859 Troy - North Adams excursion necessarily crossed them, but after 1879 the T&B's own track there ran beside the BHT&W's and which surviving track is which is unresolved. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (two to three trains each way; WS69 shows two eastbound departures from North Adams in 1869).
sources: Segment-level: 1859 from SWR59a/SWR59b; 1869 from WS69; 1880-1887 contract and 1 Feb 1887 end from GOV87; T&B operator from WP-TG and AR; Southern Vermont purchase from NCS; headway estimated. Compiled in research/branches/troy_and_greenfield_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-16).

segments.note: Report block [2] (with [3] folded in, as the report advises). Greenfield - Shelburne Falls (13.5 mi) opened 1 Jan 1868: 'two daily trains will be run between Boston and Shelburne Falls ... The Troy and Greenfield railroad will be run by the Vermont and Massachusetts railroad' (Worcester Daily Spy 1 Jan 1868); 'opened for traffic on the 1st inst. It is operated by the Vermont and Massachusetts line' (New-York Tribune 28 Jan 1868); Greenfield departures 12.20 and 4.25 pm (SWR 11 Jan 1868). Shelburne Falls - Hoosac Tunnel: regular trips from Monday 10 Aug 1868, passengers taken on to North Adams by stage over the mountain (SWR 8 Aug 1868); V&M timetable 'for Hoosac Tunnel, North Adams, and Troy' from 17 Aug 1868 (WS 17 Aug 1868) and again June 1869 (WS 10 Jul 1869). Ends when the State Manager took 'formal control' on 1 Jul 1875 (Portland Daily Press 2 Jul 1875). OPERATOR CAVEAT: the Fitchburg leased the V&M in 1874 (Wikipedia, month not found), so for 1874 - Jun 1875 these may have been Fitchburg (V&M Division) trains; the colour, not the years, is what is uncertain (report block [3], UNRESOLVED 1). headway_min is SOURCED at about two trains each way daily (SWR68a, WS69), expressed as 480 min.

segments.note: Report block [5]. A STATE-RUN RAILROAD: under Acts 1875 c.77 the Commonwealth's Manager (Prescott) 'assumed formal control of the Troy and Greenfield Railroad and the Hoosac Tunnel' on 1 Jul 1875, headquarters at Greenfield (Portland Daily Press 2 Jul 1875), and booked State passenger receipts and wages: August 1875 '$2479 from passengers', wages $3256 (SWR 8 Oct 1875); October 1875 'a falling off in passengers' (WS 9 Dec 1875). Connecting roads could run their own trains over it on equal tolls (Governor's message 1887). Ends with the Acts 1880 c.261 operating contracts (month not found), after which 'the operating roads bore the transportation expenses' (GOV87). OPERATOR CAVEAT: a Dec 1875 advertisement still offers 'V. & M. trains for Athol, Greenfield, Hoosac Tunnel' (Worcester Daily Press 31 Dec 1875) -- how much of the traffic was the State's own trains and how much the Fitchburg's (V&M Division) through trains on tolls is NOT settled (UNRESOLVED 1). headway_min is an ESTIMATE.

segments.note: Report block [7]. The Troy and Greenfield Railroad and Hoosac Tunnel was consolidated with the Fitchburg 'on and after the first day of February, A.D. 1887' (Articles of Consolidation, Art. I, in the Governor's message of 9 Feb 1887), so the Fitchburg now owned and ran it: the 'Hoosac Tunnel Route', Boston - Troy and Boston - Rotterdam Junction - West Shore. Anchors: 1893 Boston - Chicago sleeping cars via the Hoosac Tunnel (BHT&W research file); 1894 Fitchburg excursion to Saratoga 'from Greenfield and stations west' (Bennington Banner 3 Aug 1894); every station Greenfield - Williamstown appears in Fowler's 1894 Pathfinder index. Ends at the Boston and Maine lease of the Fitchburg from 1 Jul 1900. Overlaps the contract-era Fitchburg feature in 1887 only, the year of the change (the same company ran the same trains). headway_min is an ESTIMATE.

segments.note: Report block [8]. The Boston and Maine leased the Fitchburg from 1 Jul 1900 and ran this as part of its Fitchburg Division Boston - Troy main: from 15 May 1926 the Minute Man (Wikipedia, citing the North Adams Transcript of 4 May 1926). 1951: the Feb 1952 Official Guide's Hoosac Tunnel & Wilmington table prints connections at Hoosac Tunnel station with B&M Nos. 51 (W 6.50 am), 57 (W 3.44 pm), 54 (E 9.48 am) and 60 (E 4.18 pm), and the B&M through-car list carries Minute Man coaches Boston - Troy. The tunnel was electrified c.1911-1946 and single-tracked in 1957 (Wikipedia). The Minute Man last ran 18 Jan 1958 and from 19 Jan 1958 Williamstown was the terminus, served by unnamed RDC trains; passenger service west of Greenfield ended in 1958 -- 30 Dec 1958 per Wikipedia (Fitchburg Railroad) and American-Rails, 28 Nov 1958 per American-Rails' Hoosac Tunnel reference, 'later that year' per Wikipedia (Minute Man) citing the North Adams Transcript of 8 Nov 1958; the DAY is a recorded source conflict, the year is not. Freight continued and continues (Guilford / Pan Am, Pan Am Southern 2009, CSX 2022) -- context only, not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE: the four 1951 train numbers at Hoosac Tunnel are a floor, not a count.

Compiled in research/branches/troy_and_greenfield_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-16).

segments.note: Report block [9]. Boston and Maine from the 1 Jul 1900 lease of the Fitchburg; the Boston - Troy trains (from 1926 the Minute Man) ran on west of Williamstown over the BHT&W-built track to Johnsonville and Troy. Passenger service here ended on 18 Jan 1958, the Minute Man's last run; from 19 Jan 1958 the B&M's trains were cut back from Troy to Williamstown (Wikipedia, Fitchburg Railroad and Minute Man). Drawn to 1958 because that is the year of the last train, matching the neighbouring BHT&W-layer feature; the eleven-month difference from Greenfield - Williamstown is why this is a separate feature. headway_min is an ESTIMATE.

segments.note: Report block [12], drawn as an [ANCHOR]: ONE public two-day excursion, 24-25 Oct 2015, Albany - East Deerfield and return through the Hoosac Tunnel, 11 cars behind Amtrak P42DC 145 / P40DC 822 (photographed at North Adams, railpictures.net). This is NOT regular service: the line had been freight-only since 1958 and returned to freight-only afterwards. No other year is claimed, and none should be added without its own evidence. Amtrak billed it 'the first passenger train through the tunnel in 30 years', implying a c.1985 special that was not found (UNRESOLVED 9). MEDIUM CONFIDENCE ON THE YEAR: the announcement page does not print the year; 2015 comes from secondary and photo sources. headway_min 1440 = one round trip a day on the two days.
